stem: A workshop produces chairs (x) and tables (y). Each chair requires 2 hours of carpentry and 1 hour of finishing. Each table requires 3 hours of carpentry and 2 hours of finishing. Available hours per week: carpentry 18, finishing 10. At least 2 chairs must be produced. Which of the following feasible production plans has the greatest total number of units (x + y)?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Feasible (carpentry 8+9=17<=18; finishing 4+6=10<=10; x=4>=2) but total=7 is not maximum.
Carpentry: 2(6)+3(2)=12+6=18<=18. Finishing: 6+2(2)=10<=10. x=6>=2. Total=8. All constraints satisfied and total is maximum.

explanation: Check each candidate against all three constraints: 2x+3y<=18, x+2y<=10, x>=2. Options 3 and 4 are infeasible. Among feasible options 1 (total 7) and 2 (total 8), option 2 has the higher total.

explanation_sections.punchline: Eliminate infeasible points first, then maximise the objective among survivors.
explanation_sections.approach: Two-pass: (1) compute 2x+3y and x+2y for each point; eliminate any exceeding 18 or 10 respectively. (2) Among survivors, pick the highest x+y. Options 3 and 4 fail step 1. Option 2 beats option 1 in total.
explanation_sections.lesson: A candidate with a higher objective value that violates a constraint cannot be selected. Feasibility gates optimisation.
explanation_sections.timing: 80 s. Filter infeasible in 30 s, compare totals in 10 s.
